title: Alternatives to Prague: 5 quieter cities and towns
author: Brogan
intro: Prague is beautiful, cheap to fly to and very, very busy. If you want the same mix of old squares, castles and good-value beer with fewer people, these five places come closest.
seo_description: Wrocław, Kraków, Ljubljana, Bratislava and Český Krumlov give you Prague's old towns, castles and value with fewer crowds. How each compares.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Most like Prague:** Kraków
- **Quietest city:** Wrocław
- **Prettiest small town:** Český Krumlov
- **Greenest:** Ljubljana
- **Easiest add-on:** Bratislava

All five have a medieval or baroque old town, a river and cheap food and drink by Western European standards. Most have direct flights from the UK, and the rest are easy to reach from a nearby airport.

sections.heading: How they compare
sections.text:
| Place | Feel | Nights | Getting there |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kraków | Big, lively, historic | 3 to 4 | Direct flights from many UK airports |
| Wrocław | Relaxed, riverside | 2 to 3 | Direct flights from several UK airports |
| Ljubljana | Small, green, car-free centre | 2 to 3 | Fewer direct flights; Venice and Zagreb are alternatives |
| Bratislava | Compact, castle on the hill | 1 to 2 | About an hour from Vienna |
| Český Krumlov | Fairytale small town | 1 to 2 | About three hours from Prague |

If Prague's draw for you is the grand scale and the nightlife, Kraków is the closest match. If it's the pretty old streets, Český Krumlov or Ljubljana will feel more special and much calmer.

sections.heading: Kraków: the closest match
sections.text:
[Kraków](/destinations/krakow) is the one to pick if you want a big, historic, lively city break. Its main square is one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, Wawel Castle sits on a hill above the river, and the old Jewish quarter of Kazimierz is full of bars and cafés.

It isn't empty, but it's spread out enough that it rarely feels as packed as Prague's Old Town Square and Charles Bridge.

- **Day trips:** the Wieliczka salt mine and Auschwitz-Birkenau.
- **Busiest:** summer, and December, when the Christmas market fills the main square.

Our [Budapest or Krakow at Christmas](/blog/budapest-or-krakow-at-christmas) post compares it with another favourite.

sections.heading: Wrocław and Ljubljana: the calm ones
sections.text:
[Wrocław](/destinations/wroclaw), in western Poland, has a colourful main square to rival Prague's, a cathedral island with gas lamps lit by hand at dusk, and hundreds of little bronze dwarf statues hidden around the streets. It has a fraction of the visitors.

Local knowledge: hunting for Wrocław's dwarfs is a good way to explore. The tourist office sells a map, and there are well over 600 of them now.

[Ljubljana](/destinations/ljubljana), the Slovenian capital, is smaller still. Its old town has been closed to cars for years, so it's a pleasure to walk, with cafés along the river, a castle on the hill above and the lakes and mountains of Slovenia an hour away.

sections.heading: Bratislava and Český Krumlov: short stays
sections.text:
[Bratislava](/destinations/bratislava), the Slovak capital, is compact: a small old town, a white castle above the Danube and some quirky statues. Most people find a day or two enough, so it works best combined with [Vienna](/destinations/vienna), an hour away by train or boat.

[Český Krumlov](/destinations/cesky-krumlov) is a little Czech town wrapped in a loop of the Vltava river, with a huge castle and red-roofed streets that look like a film set. It's a popular day trip from Prague, so stay the night to see it after the coach tours leave.

Tip: if you love Prague but hate the crowds, combine them. Spend two nights in Prague, then two in Český Krumlov, which is about three hours away by bus.

sections.heading: When Prague is still the right choice
sections.text:
None of these has quite Prague's mix of grand architecture, galleries, music and nightlife in one place. If it's your first trip to Central Europe, Prague is still worth seeing, and you can avoid the worst of the crowds.

- **Go in the shoulder season:** early spring or late autumn is much calmer than summer.
- **Get up early:** Charles Bridge at 7am is a different place from Charles Bridge at noon.
- **Stay outside the Old Town:** Malá Strana or Vinohrady are quieter in the evening.

Our [Prague in 3 days](/blog/prague-in-3-days) plan has the details, and [Vienna or Prague at Christmas](/blog/vienna-or-prague-at-christmas) compares two winter favourites.

sections.heading: Still deciding?
sections.text:
Our [3-day city break](/blog/best-places-for-a-3-day-city-break-in-europe) post has more ideas, and the [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page lists every city we cover. For more quieter swaps, see our alternatives to [Barcelona](/blog/alternatives-to-barcelona) and [Dubrovnik](/blog/alternatives-to-dubrovnik).

If you can't agree, add Prague and a couple of these to [somewhere.party](/) and let the draw pick.

faqs.question: What city is most like Prague?
faqs.answer: Kraków is the closest: a big historic old town, a castle above the river, good nightlife and low prices, with fewer crowds.

faqs.question: Is Kraków less busy than Prague?
faqs.answer: Generally, yes. Kraków is busy in summer and at Christmas, but its old town is more spread out and rarely as packed as Prague's centre.

faqs.question: Is Český Krumlov worth visiting from Prague?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it's about three hours each way, so stay the night if you can. The town is much calmer once the day tours leave.

faqs.question: Can you do Bratislava in a day?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bratislava's old town and castle can be seen in a day, which is why many people visit it from Vienna, an hour away.
